item.title: #3586617: Filter subcontext children by view access and hard scope
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 12 files, +868/−16 · php +821/−6 · md +43/−8 · yml +2 · sh +2/−2
  • Diff: f7c59f4
  • Discussion: #3586617 · 1 contributor · 16 comments

Summary

Subcontext children are now checked before they are delivered with a selected parent. Previously a child with its own scope, for example Roles = Editor, was delivered to every account that received the parent. Children the current user cannot view, or whose delivered translation is not published, were also delivered. This affected the selector path, the Load tool, and the conditional decision prompt sent to the AI provider. Children that fail the checks are now dropped, and they are no longer sent to the provider. Sites that relied on a custom-scope child reaching users outside its scope must change that child's scope.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Security: Closes an access leak where subcontext children with their own scope, denied view access, or unpublished delivered translations were delivered with the parent and sent to the AI provider.
  • New API: AiContextSubcontextResolver::resolve() accepts optional $langcode and $cacheability arguments.

Technical details

The cause was that AiContextSubcontextResolver::batchLoadChildren() uses accessCheck(TRUE), which does nothing for this entity type because context items have no query access handler. The published query also matches a child when any translation is published. The fix adds a private filterDeliverableChildren() step in resolve(), run before any conditional AI decision. For each child it takes the translation the caller will deliver (AiContextLanguageService::translateItem()). It drops the child if that translation is unpublished, then if access('view') is not allowed. The publication check comes first because administrators, accounts with the unpublished-view permission, and owners pass the view check on a draft. A loop is used instead of translateItems() because that method checks access as a boolean and would lose the access cacheability.

Children with their own scope (inheritsParentScope() is FALSE) are then passed through AiContextScopeResolverInterface::filterByRequestContext(). Children that inherit the parent scope are not re-filtered, because the parent was already selected, including through Always include or Load. A child in the Always include list skips hard filters but still needs view access. The Load tool has no Always include list, so it hard-filters every own-scope child.

resolve() gains optional ?string $langcode and ?CacheableMetadata $cacheability parameters. When $langcode is NULL it is detected. AiContextSelector passes the detected language and its cache metadata, so child access results merge into the selection result. LoadAiContextItemById passes its language. The language is added to the conditional decision cache key, so decisions differ per language. The service definition gains @ai_context.scope_resolver and @ai_context.language_service constructor arguments. Docs in docs/features/subcontext.md were updated.

Upgrade

If you construct AiContextSubcontextResolver manually (the service definition is updated), pass two new constructor arguments after the provider config resolver: AiContextScopeResolverInterface $scopeResolver and AiContextLanguageService $languageService. Callers of resolve() can optionally pass a language code and a CacheableMetadata accumulator:

$resolver->resolve($parents, $always_include, $never_include, $task, $langcode, $cache_metadata);

item.title: #3583039: A failed result's output values are unreachable through getOutputValue()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +280/−30 · php +264/−18 · md +16/−12
  • Diff: 784162c
  • Discussion: #3583039 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

When a tool returns ExecutableResult::failure() with values, those values can now be read through $tool->getOutputValue() and getOutputValues(). Before, only a success published outputs. A caller using the documented accessor after a failure got a ContextException, and the values were reachable only through getResult()->getContextValues(). A failure can still be partial: a required output it does not carry stays unset, and getOutputValue() still throws for that one. drush tool:run now prints the outputs a failed tool carried.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: After execute(), a failed result's declared values are published as outputs, readable via getOutputValue(); getOutputValues() skips unset outputs on a failed result instead of throwing.

Technical details

ToolBase::execute() no longer returns early from its catch blocks. After any path, it resets $this->outputs and copies result context values whose keys are declared in output_definitions, for failures as well as successes. On a success, a setOutputValue() exception still propagates. On a failure, a value its output cannot store (for example a string for a list output) is logged with Error::logException() and left out, so the tool's own failure message is not hidden by an exception. A @todo notes that the formatted result still carries such a value (work item 3583124). failOnOutputViolations() still runs only on success. When it converts a success into a Runtime failure, it now also clears the outputs, so rejected values are not readable.

TypedOutputsTrait::getOutputValues() checks whether the tool is a ToolInterface with a result whose status is false. If so, it catches the ContextException for an unset required output and omits that key. In every other case it still throws. The TypedOutputsInterface docblocks now say that a failure's outputs may be partial. ToolRunCommand drops its comment saying a failed tool carries no output values. It already reads getFormattedResult()->getContextValues(), so a failure's values now appear in its output. The agent docs and the drush docs were updated to match. Kernel and drush tests were added, using a new partial_failure_tool test plugin.

Upgrade

Callers that guarded output reads with if ($tool->getResultStatus()) because a failure would throw can now read a failure's outputs. They should expect a required output to be missing on a failure. Use getOutputValues(), which skips unset outputs on a failure, or catch ContextException around getOutputValue().

item.title: #3583097: Rebuilt input violations pass the cause where the constraint goes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +198/−6 · php +198/−6
  • Diff: ec33b04
  • Discussion: #3583097 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

Violations returned by a tool's validateInputs() now keep their constraint. A required input with no value reports a NotNull constraint, so callers can tell it apart from a Choice or other failure by calling getConstraint(). A kernel test now covers this for top-level inputs, list items and map properties.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The issue described a bug in the code that rebuilds violations to put the input name on the property path. It passed getCause() where ConstraintViolation::__construct() expects the constraint, so getConstraint() returned NULL. The commit message and the new test's docblock say the constructor argument fix for validateInputValues() and the list item and map walkers landed with #3583065. The diff for this commit therefore contains only the remaining gap in TypedInputsTrait::validateInputValues(). The special-case violation for a required input with a NULL value, which replaces the typed-data detail with an instruction, now passes new NotNull() as the constraint argument. It still carries the entity type check code from #3583083 for single entity inputs.

The commit adds RebuiltViolationConstraintTest, a kernel test that goes through validateInputs(). It checks the constraint class and the property path (for example subject.1, subject.status, subject.rows.1.status) for NotNull and Choice failures. It also checks that two failures on one tool report different constraint classes.

item.title: #3586646: Document the entity_context keys as public API and how to pull context from background jobs
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +125/−0 · md +115 · php +10
  • Diff: 9418fb5
  • Discussion: #3586646 · 1 contributor · 21 comments

Summary

The 1.0.0 docs for AI Context now state which request metadata keys are stable public API. They also explain how a queue worker, cron hook or Drush command can pull context. Integrators such as Content Studio can depend on this behavior. The docs also say that pull ignores the push gates and writes no usage record. They say that usage records list items selected before the token budget is applied. This is a documentation and docblock change only. No behavior changed.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: The entity_context request metadata keys (entity type, entity ID, bundle, path, plus the top-level path fallback) are now documented as public API.

Technical details

docs/developers/api-stability.md gets a "Request metadata keys" section. It lists the accepted entity_context keys: entity_type, entity_type_id or type; entity_id or id; bundle; and path, with a top-level path fallback. The keys are set with InputBase::setRequestMetadataValue(). Setting entity_context again replaces the whole array. A numeric entity ID is cast to int, and a UUID or other string ID is ignored. Bundle and path are untrusted string-matching hints that never load an entity or grant access. Adding an alias is not a break. Removing one or tightening a rule is. The reader class AiContextProviderRequestContextFactory stays @internal.

docs/developers/consumer_api.md gets a "Background jobs and queue workers" section built around ai_context.selection_factory and fromConsumer(). It documents these points:

  • Item queries use accessCheck(TRUE), so the account running the job decides what is selected. Cron runs as anonymous and usually selects nothing.
  • Only saved entities can be passed through the public pull API.
  • Entity context persists on the current request across pulls.
  • Conditional subcontext (conditional_subcontext_enabled, conditional_max_parents) can make its own AI calls, and it is a site-wide setting.
  • Pull writes no usage record.
  • Pull does not enforce push_enabled, the type kill switch or isAvailable(). Callers can use isPushAllowed() if they want those honored.

The AiContextSelectionFactoryInterface::fromConsumer() docblock now says the same about the push gates and usage records, and points to #3586600 for planned pull usage records. docs/features/usage_tracking.md says usage records show items selected before rendering, including ones the token budget shortened or dropped. #3586645 tracks that.

Upgrade

Contrib code that reads context from a background job can use the documented pull pattern:

$factory = \Drupal::service('ai_context.selection_factory');
$selection = $factory->fromConsumer('my_type:my_instance', $task, 'node', $nid);
$context = $factory->getResultFromSelection($selection)->getRenderedText();

Run the job as an account that holds Use Published AI Context in AI Features.

Contribution

  • Opened: October 22, 2026
  • Committed: November 3, 2026 (12 days later)

item.title: #3586649: Uninstalling Dynamic Entity Reference deletes Specific Entities values and removes the item restriction
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 15 files, +1581/−14 · php +1467/−1 · md +100/−13 · yml +13 · json +1
  • Diff: 8a075d5
  • Discussion: #3586649 · 1 contributor · 41 comments

Summary

Uninstalling Dynamic Entity Reference (DER) used to silently delete every Specific Entities value on AI Context items, in all revisions. Reinstalling DER did not bring the values back. Items that had been limited to specific entities then matched everywhere. The uninstall is now blocked while any context item has Specific Entities values on its current revision or on a pending draft. The message lists up to five affected items. Old revisions do not block the uninstall. Instead, after a successful uninstall each old revision that held values gets a revision log note listing the entities it referenced (type, ID, label), so you can re-enter the values by hand. Values are not restored automatically. The docs, including the Specific Entities section of scopes.md, are corrected.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: AiContextDynamicEntityReferenceSetup gains getItemIdsWithValues(), countItemsWithValues(), getInstalledFieldName(), prepareRevisionLogNotes(), writePendingRevisionLogNotes(), recoverConfirmedRevisionLogNotes(), collectRevisionLogNotes() and writeRevisionLogNotes(). The module also adds hook_module_preuninstall() handling for dynamic_entity_reference.

Technical details

entity_items is a base field provided by dynamic_entity_reference, so core drops its storage on uninstall. AiContextUninstallValidator now handles dynamic_entity_reference. It calls AiContextDynamicEntityReferenceSetup::getItemIdsWithValues(), which combines default revisions, latest revisions, and pending drafts of any translation. It returns reasons as TranslatableMarkup so core's template does not double-escape labels. If the check throws, it returns NULL, the validator blocks the uninstall, and the error is logged. The legacy target_entities field name is supported via getInstalledFieldName().

Old revisions are handled in two phases. ai_context_module_preuninstall() calls prepareRevisionLogNotes(), which stores notes in State under ai_context.dynamic_entity_reference_uninstall_prepared_notes. Nothing is written yet, because the uninstall might still fail. ai_context_modules_uninstalled() runs only after success. It calls writePendingRevisionLogNotes(), which promotes the prepared notes to ai_context.dynamic_entity_reference_uninstall_notes and appends them to the revision log. It uses a direct database update, so presave hooks such as scope cleanup and moderation do not run. It then resets the entity cache and invalidates the item cache tags. This also runs during config sync.

If the write fails, the error is logged, the confirmed notes stay in State, and the other uninstall hooks still run. ai_context_cron() retries confirmed notes through recoverConfirmedRevisionLogNotes(). A later DER uninstall writes any confirmed notes before it captures new ones, and stops if that write fails. Unconfirmed prepared notes are never written by cron. ai_context_uninstall() deletes both State keys. The Revisions overview form now wraps the log in nl2br() so multi-line notes display. A test module, ai_context_der_uninstall_test, simulates load and write failures. The diff I read omits the kernel test file.

Upgrade

Before uninstalling Dynamic Entity Reference, clear the Specific Entities values on any context item that uses them. Check pending drafts too. Otherwise the uninstall page, Drush and config import will refuse to remove the module. After the uninstall, old revisions that held values have a revision log note listing the referenced entities. Re-enter the values from those notes if you need them. Run cron before uninstalling DER a second time after reinstalling it, so Drupal purges the deleted field storage.

Contribution

  • Opened: October 22, 2026
  • Committed: November 3, 2026 (12 days later)

item.title: #3594659: Multimodal evaluation: support file inputs (images, documents) in datasets
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 37 files, +1896/−43 · php +1814/−34 · md +53/−5 · yml +19/−3 · txt +9 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: 8912f1e
  • Discussion: #3594659 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

AI Eval dataset questions can now include images (png, jpeg, webp, gif). Chat targets, config agent targets and AI Prompt workflow targets send the images to the model. LLM judges receive the same images when grading. You add images with a new Upload images field in the question editor, or by listing filename and image reference pairs under Files. A model or judge that cannot read images does not get a zero: the question is skipped, or the judge returns no score, and the reason is shown. Other workflow runners and code-defined agents skip image questions. The results page shows thumbnails of a question's images and any skip reason. Limits are 5 MB per image and 5 images per question.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: Uploaded question images become managed files under private://ai_eval/question-files/ (or public:// when private storage is not configured).
  • New API: New services ai_eval.question_image_resolver (QuestionImageResolver) and ai_eval.question_image_upload (QuestionImageUpload); WorkflowRunOptions carries an images list to workflow runners.

Technical details

The per-question files key already existed in the dataset schema but the runner ignored it. A new QuestionImageResolver service turns files entries into images and attaches them to the last user ChatMessage. It accepts public:// and private:// URIs and data:image/...;base64, URLs with a matching MIME type. For FileSource YAML datasets, FileSource also rewrites paths relative to the YAML file, and the resolved path, symlinks included, must stay inside that folder. Remote URLs are refused. Non-image string values are carried but never sent.

EvalRunner resolves images before invoking the target. It skips the row (unscored, with skip_reason) when the model cannot read images, when the workflow runner is not ai_prompt, or when a code-defined agent is used. For config agents (AiAgentEntityWrapper) it checks the agent's provider and model, falling back to the chat_with_tools default. If the model cannot be resolved, it sends the images anyway and records an image_warning. AiPromptWorkflowRunner attaches $options->images to the rendered prompt. The LlmJudge base class receives the same resolved bytes through a _question_images entry in the grader context, so judges see what the target saw. A judge without vision support returns a null score with an explanation.

Uploads go through QuestionImageUpload, which stores managed files and tracks usage. The question editor saves inside a database transaction and deletes the new files on failure. A new QuestionFileUsageHooks releases file usage when a question is deleted. Run identity records each image's name, SHA-256, MIME type and byte count in a files entry, not the contents. Results pages limit inline previews to 256 KB each and 2 MB per page, and show the name and size when a preview is too large. LabeledExample gained a files map. HumanLabelSource reloads a question's files from the source dataset only when PromotionService::sourceDataset() reports an exact match with the run. Otherwise that review is left out of judge validation, and inexactAnnotationCount() feeds a message on the validation page. Text-only reviews stay usable after the dataset changes or is deleted.

Upgrade

Custom classes that construct AiPromptWorkflowRunner need the extra constructor argument, which is optional on the class:

arguments: ['@entity_type.manager', '@?ai.provider', '@ai_eval.chat_invoker', '@ai_eval.rate_limit_handler', '@datetime.time', '@ai_eval.question_image_resolver']

EvalRunner, EvalResultsController, FileSource, HumanLabelSource and LlmJudge also take the new service or @ai_eval.promotion_service. Constructor changes only matter if you subclass or re-register them.

Contribution

  • Opened: June 18, 2026
  • Committed: November 3, 2026 (4 months later)

item.title: #3594869: ai_eval_droost: move to Droost 2 and Tool API, and fix two false passes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 19 files, +1006/−243 · php +924/−172 · md +65/−63 · yml +9/−6 · json +5/−2 · txt +3
  • Diff: 4be97e8
  • Discussion: #3594869 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The ai_eval_droost submodule now grades built Drupal state through Droost 2 and Tool API instead of the old MCP Server plugins. On a Droost 2 site the old code could not reach any tool. Droost 1 support is dropped. Two false passes are fixed: a Canvas read with no item list used to count as an empty tree, so component_present with count: 0 passed. A failed View configuration read used to leave unfiltered assertions free to run and pass. Both now fail with a reason. View specs can only be graded from Drush (drush aer), because Droost 2 refuses build tools in a web request. Canvas and View row reads from the admin UI use the logged-in user's access. A site that updates ai_eval while still on Droost 1 keeps working, and the status page reports the missing requirement.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: ai_eval_droost now requires drupal/droost 2.0.0 or later and drupal/tool (1.0.0-beta12 or later); Droost 1 and MCP Server are no longer supported.
  • API change: DroostOracle constructor now takes the gateway, entity type manager, logger and an optional SAPI string; new DroostToolGatewayInterface; DroostOracleInterface::ALLOWED_TOOLS shrunk to six tools.
  • New API: New ai_eval_droost.tool_gateway service (ToolApiGateway, implementing DroostToolGatewayInterface) and a runtime requirements check on the status page.

Technical details

Tools now run through a new ToolApiGateway (service ai_eval_droost.tool_gateway) behind DroostToolGatewayInterface, because Tool API's runner classes are final and tests need their own interface. The gateway takes @?tool.runner, so the container still compiles without Tool API. It calls ToolRunner::run() and returns a {success, message, data, category} envelope. The data value comes from the result's data context value, and messages are reduced to plain text. A missing tool, Tool API input and access failures, and exceptions all come back as envelopes rather than throwing.

DroostOracle keeps its fixed allowlist, now cut to droost_views_get, droost_views_execute, droost_canvas_tree_get, droost_canvas_tree_validate and droost_entity_load. Under the cli and phpdbg SAPIs it loads user 1 and passes it as the account, as drush droost:tool does. Otherwise it passes no account, so Tool API uses the current user. It rewrites failure messages: a missing tool names its providing module (droost_build or droost_canvas), access denials say which account was used, and a build-tool refusal gets "Grade this spec from Drush (drush aer)." appended. A data value that is not an array is a failure.

In AssertionRunner, a new failTarget() helper emits one failure per assertion, keeping each assertion's id and tier. It is used when droost_views_get fails and when droost_canvas_tree_get succeeds without an items array. Malformed-assertion failures are still reported. A new DroostRequirements hook (runtime_requirements) errors when Droost or Tool API is missing or Droost is older than 2.0.0, and warns when the Droost version cannot be determined, as in a dev checkout. Tests added: a rewritten unit test using FakeGateway, new false-pass tests, and a kernel ToolApiGatewayTest against real Droost 2. verify_live.php now resolves its expected node ids from the dataset UUIDs, and CI runs the ai_eval_droost group.

Upgrade

Install the new dependencies before updating the submodule:

composer require drupal/droost:^2.0 drupal/tool:^1.0@beta

Enable droost_build for View specs and droost_canvas for Canvas specs. Run View specs from Drush (drush aer). Custom code that constructs DroostOracle directly must pass the new arguments: the gateway, @entity_type.manager and the logger.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: November 2, 2026
  • Committed: November 3, 2026

item.title: #3594873: Agent tests send a wrapped task instead of the chat messages the site sends
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +349/−23 · php +329/−16 · md +20/−7
  • Diff: d81430c
  • Discussion: #3594873 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Agent tests in ai_eval now give config agents the question as separate chat messages with their roles, as the AI Assistant does on the site. Before, the question was flattened into one text and wrapped as a task ("Task Title… Task Description…"), and HTML in it was stripped. Scores for agent tests can change, including for single-turn questions, so thresholds and baselines may need re-checking. Code-defined agents that read only the Task still get the flattened transcript.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

EvalRunner::invokeAgent() now takes the normalized ChatMessage[] that runQuestionBody() already builds, in addition to the flattened transcript. It keeps setTask(new Task($message)), because code-defined agents read only the Task, and also calls setChatInput(new ChatInput($conversationTail)). Config agents build their history from the chat input, so they get the original turns with roles. The agent's own system prompt, or an optimizer's agent_prompt_override candidate, stays in force.

Dataset system entries are dropped. The filter was extracted from the chat path into a private withoutQuestionSystemMessages() and is shared by chat and agent modes. It logs the drop once, outside the rate-limit retry closure.

A new kernel test, EvalRunnerAgentChatInputTest, uses a real config agent with a scripted provider. It covers three-turn roles with the caller prefix, single-turn HTML without a Task wrapper, system-entry removal with the override prompt, and a tool loop that keeps the original turns once. The CHANGELOG gets an "Unreleased / Fixed" entry. docs/user/usage/datasets.md and schema/README.md no longer say agent mode flattens.

Upgrade

No code changes are needed. Re-run agent tests and re-baseline scores and thresholds, since input to config agents differs from earlier versions.

item.title: #3586573: Add setting to add CCC to main menu
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 22 files, +1103/−6 · php +1018/−2 · md +43 · yml +29/−1 · css +12/−3 · json +1
  • Diff: 1a45fa2
  • Discussion: #3586573 · 1 contributor · 44 comments

Summary

Context Control Center can now optionally appear as its own item in the main admin menu instead of only under Configuration > AI. It is off by default. On the General settings page, above "Show overview page", a new "Add to main menu" checkbox turns it on, and a "Menu item title" field (default "Context") appears when it is checked. The item uses a stack icon and links to the existing CCC redirect, so it opens the overview page when that is enabled and the context items list otherwise. With Navigation (Drupal CMS) it shows in the sidebar after Media; with Toolbar only it shows at the top level after Content. Existing sites get the new settings from a post-update, and the item stays off until an admin enables it.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Database update: Post-update ai_context_post_update_0016_add_main_menu_settings adds the two keys to existing sites; the item stays off.
  • Config change: New ai_context.settings keys main_menu_enabled (default false) and main_menu_title (default Context), both optional in schema; title has NotBlank, max 255 and no < or > constraints.

Technical details

The link is provided by a menu link deriver, AiContextMainMenuLinkDeriver, declared as plugin ai_context.main_menu_item in ai_context.links.menu.yml (class MenuLinkDefault). It returns nothing unless main_menu_enabled is on. With the navigation module installed the link goes in the content menu (weight 10); otherwise it goes in admin under system.admin (weight -9). When both are installed it appears in Navigation only. The title is stripped of tags and falls back to a translatable "Context" when it is empty or equals the default; a custom title is not translated. The existing ai_context.main_menu_link under Configuration is kept, and its plugin ID is retained so overrides and styling still apply.

AiContextSettingsConfigSubscriber now takes router.builder and calls setRebuildNeeded() when the toggle changes, or when the title changes while the toggle is on. Core rebuilds menu links on a router rebuild, so no drush cr is needed. The settings form calls rebuildIfNeeded() in submit so the redirect shows the change. ai_context_toolbar_alter() adds the config:system.menu.admin cache tag to the Toolbar tray, so a user whose tray was empty does not keep a cached empty tray after the item is enabled.

Validation: the schema marks both keys requiredKey: false, so older exports still import. The title carries NotBlank, Length (255) and a Regex that rejects < and >, because Navigation inserts the title into an HTML tooltip. The form only requires the title while the toggle is on. While it is off, a blank title keeps the saved one, tags are stripped, and a still-invalid title becomes "Context". The form reads defaults from the editable config, not the overridden config, so settings.php overrides are not written back on save. CSS adds the icon for the new link's toolbar classes and an .ai-context-settings-nested indent.

The diff also changes AiContextScopeBase::buildValueForm() to run option labels through Html::escape, so a role label containing markup no longer breaks the value form. This is unrelated to the menu setting.

Upgrade

Run database updates (drush updb). ai_context_post_update_0016_add_main_menu_settings adds main_menu_enabled: false and main_menu_title: Context to ai_context.settings if missing. Existing values are left alone. Export the config afterwards to keep it complete. To show the item, enable "Add to main menu" at /admin/config/ai/context/settings/general.

item.title: #3586603: Scope cleanup can leave an item published with an emptied hard-filter scope
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 22 files, +3487/−58 · php +3228/−41 · md +241/−17 · yml +18
  • Diff: d3d7bc4

Summary

Scope cleanup no longer leaves an item published with an emptied scope. Before, deleting a role (or language, term, bundle, referenced entity, or uninstalling a module) could remove the last value limiting a context item, so an item limited to the "Reviewer" role was suddenly delivered to every user, with no log or message. Now cleanup unpublishes such an item (state Archived on the ai_context_editorial workflow), saves a new revision explaining which value was removed, logs a warning per item, and shows the acting user one warning with a count and a link to the item list. After deleting roles, languages, terms or bundles, or uninstalling modules, check the context item list for newly unpublished or archived items. Items that stay published: Global items, items that keep at least one value, and items that only lose Context Tags (ranking only). Sites that already ran post-update 0006 on 1.0.0-beta5 or 1.0.0-rc1 do not run it again, so items it emptied earlier stay published and need manual review.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: ai_context.scope_cleanup service gains new constructor arguments (logger, messenger, current user, time, database, notice service); only relevant to code that instantiates it directly.
  • New API: AiContextItem::canUnpublishWithModerationState() (@internal) and a persisted ai_context.scope_cleanup_notice service (@internal) hold cleanup counts for one warning per request.

Technical details

The change is in AiContextScopeCleanupService. When removeScopeValuesFromItems() empties a scope, or removeEntityItemReference() removes the last Specific Entities reference, widensWhenEmptied() decides whether the item would reach more requests. The rule: any stored-value scope except Context Tags (RANKING_ONLY_SCOPES) counts as a hard filter, custom stored-value scopes included, and there is no public policy API in 1.0. Global items are never unpublished. A subcontext item with no stored inherit flag is unpublished when it would resolve to a Global parent, even if the emptied value was a tag.

Unpublishing uses setUnpublishedWithModerationState() on every published translation, saved in one database transaction. publish_on (and publish_state when present) is cleared on every translation so Scheduler cannot republish it. The save is a new revision with a log message, the current user as author, and the request time. Saves that do not unpublish use setSyncing(TRUE) so content moderation does not add a revision that copies the old log message. If a moderated workflow has no unpublished default-revision state (AiContextItem::canUnpublishWithModerationState()), the item is not saved: the stale value stays (it matches no request), an error is logged once per scope, and the warning gets an extra sentence. Already unpublished items get the stale value removed with no revision, log or message, unless they have a publish_on date, in which case it is cancelled in a new revision.

Counts live in the new ai_context.scope_cleanup_notice service, tagged persist so one warning with totals survives the container rebuild during a module uninstall. The messenger warning is skipped for the anonymous user (cron, Drush) and deferred until the surrounding transaction commits on entity delete. Post-update 0006 uses the same rule. Docs for scopes, services and custom scopes were updated, and kernel tests were added including AiContextScopeCleanupForeignValuesTest (one case per trigger) and a new ai_context_test_item_save_fail test module.

Site owners: after drush updatedb (post-update 0006), after deleting roles, languages, terms, vocabularies or bundles, or after module uninstalls, review the context item list for newly unpublished or archived items and re-check their scope before republishing. On sites that already ran 0006 on 1.0.0-beta5 or 1.0.0-rc1, review published items that have no Roles, Languages, Site Sections, Entity Types, Taxonomy Terms or Specific Entities value. Custom workflows need an unpublished state with Published cleared and Default revision selected, or cleanup will not save the item and logs an error. Custom stored-value scope authors: cleanup now treats your scope as a hard filter.

item.title: #3594867: Gold labeling still serves legacy tool steps whose output is only "assistant:"
item.description:

  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 12 files, +200/−14 · php +194/−13 · md +6/−1
  • Diff: 97e5972
  • Discussion: #3594867 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

In ai_eval 1.1.x, traces imported from AI Observability in the legacy text format could show an agent's tool step as a reply of just "assistant:". These steps were wrongly treated as final answers. They appeared on the gold labeling screen and counted toward coverage, agreement and judge validation. They are now excluded. Promoting such a step is refused, and so is promoting an embeddings call, which has no text answer to test. The trace card explains why. "Promote all" now picks the real final answer of an agent run. On the compare page, a difference that reads the same on both sides, such as a changed dataset hash, now shows once ("Dataset content: changed") instead of "A: changed; B: changed". Labels already saved on tool steps stay but are no longer counted.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: TraceBrowser::isRoleLabelOnly(), PromotionService::STATUS_TOOL_STEP and PromotionService::STATUS_NO_ANSWER outcome statuses.

Technical details

TraceBrowser::isFinalAnswer() now also requires that the reply is not role-label-only. The new TraceBrowser::isRoleLabelOnly() trims response_text and strips a leading assistant: (case-insensitive). If nothing is left, the reply is a tool step. GoldSetAgreement and HumanLabelSource inherit the fix through isFinalAnswer().

PromotionService::promotionIntegrityFlag() returns two new flags. no_answer (STATUS_NO_ANSWER) applies when response_kind is set, as for embeddings. tool_step (STATUS_TOOL_STEP) applies when the reply is role-label-only and there are no response_tools. Both count as refused in the promotion report. For agent runs, the "Promote all" selection of the last chat now calls TraceBrowser::isFinalAnswer() instead of its own text and tools check. As a result, a trailing "assistant:" step is skipped and an earlier real answer is chosen.

PromoteFragment gains toolStepNotice() and noAnswerNotice(). TraceReviewFragment renders them as a refusal_notice warning with "This trace cannot be promoted." In ResultsCompareController, the two readable values are compared as strings. When they match, a single value is shown, otherwise the "A: @a; B: @b" form is kept. The user guide and changelog are updated. Existing tests that expected embeddings to promote with an empty answer now expect a refusal.

Upgrade

No update steps are needed. Embeddings calls can no longer be promoted, so any workflow that relied on promoting them with an empty AI response will now see them refused.

item.title: #3620031: Adopt the three-tier protocol: block Restricted images, warn on Moderate
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +100/−28 · md +88/−18 · yml +10/−8 · json +2/−2
  • Diff: 2469b0d
  • Discussion: #3620031 · 2 contributors · 11 comments
  • Followers: 3
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 2 contributors

Summary

The image safety recipe now has three tiers instead of a binary block. Safe images save silently. Moderate images (partial nudity, suggestive content, mild violence) are accepted, and the uploader sees a warning. Restricted images (full nudity, explicit sexual content, gore, graphic violence, graphic medical imagery) are still blocked with a validation error. An image the model cannot classify is treated as Restricted. Sites that already applied the recipe do not pick this up automatically.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: drupal/ai_validations constraint raised from ^1.3 to ^1.4, which provides the opt-in XSAFE/XWARN/XBLOCK warning tier (#3606131).
  • Config change: Shipped field_validation.rule_set.media_image rule: new title, XSAFE/XWARN/XBLOCK prompt, reworded message, new warningMessage key in the rule data.

Technical details

The rule's prompt in config/field_validation.rule_set.media_image.yml now returns XSAFE, XWARN or XBLOCK in place of XTRUE/XFALSE. The rule title becomes "Block restricted imagery, warn on moderate". The message text now covers only Restricted content, and the new warningMessage key in the rule's data holds the Moderate text. The rule's provider is unchanged, an empty string meaning the site default. recipe.yml and the composer.json description are reworded, and composer.json requires drupal/ai_validations ^1.4.

The warning tier is opt-in in AI Validations and is active only while the warning message is non-empty. The README says that emptying it returns validation to XTRUE/XFALSE, and that the prompt must then be rewritten to match. If only one of the two is changed, uploads are blocked (empty message with the three-token prompt) or no warning is ever shown (message set with the two-token prompt). The README also documents "Adjusting the tiers", for example mapping Moderate to XBLOCK or XSAFE. It states that an XWARN verdict also writes to the ai_validations logger channel, so headless flows such as JSON:API keep an audit trail and are never blocked by a warning.

Upgrade

The recipe creates the rule set with createIfNotExists, so re-applying the new version on a site that already has the media_image rule set changes nothing. Either delete the rule set at Structure → Field Validation and re-apply the recipe, or edit the existing rule by hand:

=== DECISION ===
- If the image is SAFE, respond with: XSAFE
- If the image is MODERATE, respond with: XWARN
- If the image is RESTRICTED, respond with: XBLOCK

=== OUTPUT FORMAT ===
Respond with exactly one token — XSAFE, XWARN, or XBLOCK — and nothing else.

Then fill in the rule's Warning message field. Update drupal/ai_validations to 1.4 or newer.

Summary

The AI Eval results overview and result detail page now show the gate a run actually used. Before, they read the gate from the live test. A deleted test or a changed gate produced a threshold the run never had, often "4.0" with avg_score. The gate now comes from the settings recorded with the run. If the run has no usable record, the page uses the live test. If neither exists, the detail page says "Gate not recorded" and the overview shows the score with no "/ threshold". The same commit makes several related screen and wording fixes. The results screens show test names instead of ids (the id is kept as a hover title). The compare page uses plain labels for differences, with raw values in a closed "Technical details" section. Failure-rate rows without a failure mode are split into "Passed", "Failed, no failure mode" and "Deferred", and the shares still add up to 100%. Annotate progress counts the answers of the latest run. Calibration shows a message when a save replaced an earlier inactive fit. It also warns when the judge's rubric wording has changed, so the judge will not apply that fit. The hard and soft gate wording now says it only changes the exit code of drush ai-eval:run.

Impact

Affects front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Results overview, detail and compare screens render different text: test labels with ids as hover titles, "Gate not recorded", and a closed "Technical details" section on the compare page. Any custom theme or test that matches the old strings, such as "(untagged)" or "@done of @total suggested", needs updating.

Technical details

EvalResultsController gets a private recordedGate() helper, used by both the overview Target Health loop and detail(). It calls ResultEnvelopeBuilder::decodeValidatedSnapshot() on config_json. It accepts the snapshot's metric and threshold only when the metric parses with GateMetric::tryFrom() and the threshold is numeric. Otherwise it falls back to the live target's threshold and metric, and returns NULL if neither is available. With a NULL gate, the score cell template drops the "/ threshold" part and the aria label drops the gate comparison. The detail Gate cell prints "Gate not recorded". The detail page also prints the metric's label (for example "Pass rate") instead of the raw pass_rate. The overview now runs its pending-optimization and paged-results queries earlier and calls loadMultiple() once, so all three sections can show target labels. Cache tags for the loaded targets and ai_eval_target_list were added to the results, annotate and compare pages.

ResultsCompareController gets an optional ai_eval.grader_manager constructor argument. It adds differenceLabel() and readableValue(): hashes show as "same", "changed" or "recorded", grader ids show as grader labels, and gate metric and type are readable. The raw key and value pairs go into a closed details element titled "Technical details". FailureRateService now also groups by verdict. decorate() merges tagged verdicts back into their mode and splits only the rows with no failure mode by verdict, with labels "Passed", "Failed, no failure mode", "Deferred" or "No verdict". Result rows carry a new verdict key.

WorkflowStateService drops the fixed suggested total of 100 for the Annotate step. Progress is now the canonical annotations on the latest result over that result's question_count, and is NULL when there is no result. A new Drupal\ai_eval\Form\GateTypeWording class holds the shared gate-type labels and description for EvalTargetForm and GuidedTestForm. CalibrationSaveTrait::saveAndReport() counts inactive curves for the same provider, model and fingerprint before saving, and reports how many were replaced.
